pageCache.text:
Clubs & Wraparound Care
We offer a wide range of clubs and wraparound care between 8:00am and 6:00pm Monday to Friday, run by our dedicated staff and trusted external providers.
Timetable Autumn 2026
You have not allowed cookies and this content may contain cookies.
If you would like to view this content please Accept All Manage Cookies
Before School Clubs
There are daily clubs for morning care before the start of the school day at 8:45am. Download the Breakfast School Clubs document for details, pricing and booking information.
After School Clubs & Wraparound Care
Contact Details: Email: afterschoolcare@stoke-row.oxon.sch.uk Telephone: 07351 197030
After School Care operates from 3.15pm to 6.00pm Monday to Thursday during term time. A snack is provided for the children. The cost of a session is £14 and all bookings should be made on the After School Care Booking Form (see below).
Extra-curricular clubs are offered from 3.15 - 4.15pm as follows:
Monday – Card & Board Games for all years with games to suit all ages and interests including UNO, snap, chess, draughts, snakes and ladders and many more. Drama for year 3 – 6 is also available (please book separately with provider Berzerk Productions).
Tuesday - Craft for all years. Following on from last term we will be introducing other crafts including rock painting, origami and paper aeroplane competitions .
Wednesday - Lego for all years. This term we will be inspired by the theme of summer activities setting weekly challenges around for example beach days, summer picnics and skateparks.
Thursday – Sport for all years. The aim is to introduce sports that the children may not be familiar with.
The cost of these clubs is £7 and all bookings should be made using the Extra-Curricular Clubs Booking Form (see below).
Any child, booked into after school care from 3.15 – 6.00pm will automatically be able to attend the clubs for the first hour.
If your child is attending Drama on a Monday you can book after school care from 4.15 to 6.00pm at a cost of £10 using the After School Care Booking Form (see below).

Checkendon Pre-school

pageCache.pageTitle: Stoke Row CofE Primary School - Reading
pageCache.text:
Reading
At Stoke Row Church of England Primary School, we aim for every child to leave our school with a love of reading. Reading is central to a child’s learning, enabling them to access the curriculum but also so does so much more.
The most important thing you can do to support your child’s education is to read to/with them as much as possible.
You can search by Key stage or topic.
Oxford Owl has expert advice, top tips and activity ideas so that you can help your child with reading and maths.
Wordsforlife has lots of information about reading milestones, tips, fun activities for children to do and recommended reads for different ages.
Booktrust is the UK’s largest children’s reading charity. The website has an extensive range of resources and support to help develop a love of reading. It also has an excellent ‘Bookfinder’ which helps children to find the next book to read by entering their age and interests.
Reading Ahead is a national programme, run by The Reading Agency, which challenges you to choose six books to read, rate and review.
Yakbooks is a website full of book reviews written by children and adults. There is a very useful tool called ‘Bookchooser’, which allows you to search for different genres of books based on set criteria.
Reading develops a child’s general knowledge.

pageCache.text:
SEND
Statement on Special Educational Needs
We, at Stoke Row School, believe that every child has individual and unique needs. We also recognise that, in order to achieve their full potential, some children will require additional support. We understand that some pupils will have special educational needs at some point in their school career. Many of these pupils may require help throughout their time in school, whilst others may need a little extra support for a short period to help overcome more temporary needs. Stoke Row aims to equip all pupils with strategies for dealing with their needs in a nurturing environment which recognises that, with effort and perseverance, they can succeed. We also provide our pupils with meaningful access to the national curriculum so that they can develop a love of learning. We aim to embed a culture of high expectations so that all pupils can achieve their potential. Alongside this, we recognise the importance of developing independent working strategies in order to prepare the children for their educational journey.
Any personalised provision is designed to reflect and foster our core values of kindness, respect, perseverance, excellence and courage.
Our special education needs co-ordinator (SENDCo) is: Ms Deborah Richards
Our Governor with responsibility for SEN is: Mr Laurence Fitt
The following documents detail the provision for special educational needs at Stoke Row including access to external support agencies.
For more information, support and advice on SEN in our local area please see: https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/residents/children-education-and-families/education-and-learning/special-educational-needs-and-disability-local-offer
